won.source: Won the title by beating Ground Zero in a tourney final in Bulletin #8 at the Corestate Center, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.
Recorded as winning the title in Bulletin #16 at the Toronto Skydome, Toronto, Ontario; the sheet does not name an opponent.

Beat Universal Man in a one-night tournament final to win the vacant championship in Bulletin #22 at Wrigley Field, Chicago, Illinois. Also beat Kane Nevermor in round one and Black Mask Horror in the semi-final.
Beat Lobo the Crippler in a four-way dance in Bulletin #27 at the STW Arena, Phoenix, Arizona. The four-way also involved "Glistening" Vin Avery and Kane Nevermor.
Beat Big Dredd Vedder in Bulletin #31 at the Fleet Center, Boston, Massachusetts.
Beat Lucien Champion in Bulletin #35 at the Pontiac Silver Dome, Pontiac, Michigan.
Beat Lightning Mountain in Bulletin #40 at The Paladium, Hollywood, California.
Beat Kane Nevermor in a three-way dance in Bulletin #41 at the Civic Arena, Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. A three-way dance that also involved Lightning Mountain.

Beat The Mighty Hitman in a one-fall four-way match in Bulletin #43 at the Toronto Skydome, Toronto, Ontario. Also involved Lucien Champion and Kane Nevermor; Mercury pinned Champion with a foot on the ropes.

Beat Mercury in a four-way elimination match in Bulletin #44 at the Kiel Center, St. Louis, Missouri. Also involved the Mighty Hitman and Lightning Mountain (substituting for Kane Nevermor), a rematch from the previous show.
Recorded as winning the title in Bulletin #55, location unknown; the sheet does not name an opponent.
Recorded as winning the title in Bulletin #58, location unknown; the sheet does not name an opponent.
Recorded as winning the title in Bulletin #61, location unknown; the sheet does not name an opponent. A third reign for Lucien Champion.
Beat Lucien Champion in Bulletin #65, location unknown. Colton was the reigning World Light-Heavyweight Champion; this win unified the two titles.

Beat "Ab Fab" Adam Colton in Bulletin #67. Rush was the reigning Unified Double Crown champion; this win also took Colton's World Light-Heavyweight championship, unifying all three titles. Still champion as of Bulletin #69; STW folded shortly thereafter, and he is recorded as the league's last champion.
Won the title by beating The Celestials via forfeit in a tourney final, announced in the Commissioner's report in Bulletin #9.
Beat The Mighty Rednecks via forfeit to fill the vacant title in Bulletin #13 at the Tokyo Dome, Tokyo, Japan.
Beat The World Wide Celebrities in Bulletin #15 at the STW Arena, Phoenix, Arizona.
Beat Death Warrior & Renegade Cop in Bulletin #16 at the Toronto Skydome, Toronto, Ontario.
Beat Rick ''Rocket'' Smits & Reignman Reggie Miller in Bulletin #18 at the Tacoma Dome, Tacoma, Washington. A second reign for Death Warrior & Renegade Cop.
Beat Death Warrior & Renegade Cop in a triple threat in Bulletin #20 at Madison Square Garden, New York City. Los Dos Capones pinned The World Wide Celebrities to win the belts.
Beat Los Dos Capones in Bulletin #22 at Wrigley Field, Chicago, Illinois.
Beat Frag Master & Big Tex Williams in Bulletin #24 at the STW Arena, Phoenix, Arizona. It was during this reign the belts were renamed from the Supreme Tag Team title to the World Tag Team title.
Beat The Celestials in Bulletin #26 at the Georgia Dome, Atlanta, Georgia.

Beat Muscle Inc. in Bulletin #31 at the Fleet Center, Boston, Massachusetts. The titles were declared vacant in Bulletin #35 when The Celestials were stripped after the controversial ending of their ladder match against The Rush Brothers; The Rushes were briefly declared champions but refused the belts and that change was nulled, leaving the titles vacant.
Beat Rob Retribution in a tourney final in Bulletin #38 at the Oakland Arena, Oakland, California. Rob Retribution's own partner, Chris Crono, did not show up, having left the promotion.

Beat "Time Bomb" Blaze Colton & "Dangerous" Dave Howard in a three-way dance in Bulletin #41 at the Civic Arena, Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. The titles were declared vacant as of Bulletin #43, champions to be determined.
Beat A & A Express in Bulletin #45.
Recorded as winning the title in Bulletin #52; the sheet does not name an opponent.
Recorded as winning the title in Bulletin #53; the sheet does not name an opponent. The lineage is unknown from here until Bulletin #58.
Recorded as winning the title in Bulletin #58; the sheet does not name an opponent. The sheet does not name from whom the titles were won.
Beat Full Throttle in Bulletin #59. The last champions in the surviving record.
Recorded as the first champion winning a battle royal in Bulletin #08 at the Georgia Mountain Center, Gainesville, Georgia; the sheet does not name an opponent. The first champion.
Beat Jumpman Michael Jordan in Bulletin #11 at Cobo Hall, Detroit, Michigan.
Beat Lightning Mountain in a three-way dance in Bulletin #23 at Cobo Hall, Detroit, Michigan.
Beat King Of Extreme in Bulletin #25 at the Philadelphia Spectrum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.
Beat Bloodscream in Bulletin #26 at the Georgia Dome, Atlanta, Georgia.
Beat "Dangerous" Dave Howard in Bulletin #28 at the Houston Civic Center, Houston, Texas. A second reign for Lightning Mountain.

Beat Lightning Mountain in a title-versus-title match in Bulletin #33 at the Alamo Dome, San Antonio, Texas. Champion's own STW World Heavyweight title was also on the line. In Bulletin #34, STW officially stripped Champion of this title, since he then also held both the STW and CPW World Heavyweight titles and could not devote the time to it; he is recorded as the last title holder, as in Bulletin #35 the belt was unified with the vacant International title to form the Unified Double Crown championship.
Recorded as the first champion winning a Battle Royal in Bulletin #16 at the Toronto Skydome, Toronto, Ontario; the sheet does not name an opponent. The first champion.
Beat Big Time Player in Bulletin #18 at the Fighting Osaka Gym, Osaka, Japan.
Beat Telmeku the Mongolian Warrior in Bulletin #24 at the Toronto Skydome, Toronto, Ontario.
Beat Kerry Garret in Bulletin #27 at the STW Arena, Phoenix, Arizona.

Beat Christian ''God Damn'' Cross in a Triple Threat match in Bulletin #31 at the Fleet Center, Boston, Massachusetts. Colton pinned Dave Howard for the win. Colton was stripped in Bulletin #33 for failure to defend the title and for attacking STW officials; he is recorded as the last title holder, the belt unifying with the vacant National Television title to become part of the Unified Double Crown championship.
Won the title by beating "Time Bomb" Blaze Colton, Lobo the Crippler, and Stump Anaki in an 'Endurathon' match in Bulletin #35 at the Pontiac Silver Dome, Pontiac, Michigan.
Beat Kaos Knight at the third annual IWF pay-per-view (STW cycle #37) at Madison Square Garden, New York City.

Beat "Time Bomb" Blaze Colton in a 2-out-of-3 falls, count-anywhere match in Bulletin #39 at the MGM Grand Garden Arena, Las Vegas, Nevada. Kaos Knight won two falls to one; a second reign for Kaos Knight.
Beat Kaos Knight in Bulletin #42 at the HSBC Arena, Buffalo, New York.
Beat Hypnos in Bulletin #45 at the Alamo Dome, San Antonio, Texas. A third reign for Kaos Knight.
Beat Kaos Knight in Bulletin #47.
Beat "Mr. Attitude" Jeremy Nace in Bulletin #49.
Beat "the One" Orlando Rock in Bulletin #50.
Recorded as winning the title in Bulletin #53; the sheet does not name an opponent.

Recorded as winning the title in an unnumbered bulletin; the sheet does not name an opponent. The sheet does not give the bulletin number or an opponent for this, a second reign; the lineage is then unknown between Bulletin #55 and Bulletin #58.
Recorded as winning the title in Bulletin #59; the sheet does not name an opponent.
Recorded as winning the title in Bulletin #64; the sheet does not name an opponent.
Recorded as winning the title in Bulletin #67; the sheet does not name an opponent. A second reign for Jake Rush.
Recorded as winning the title in Bulletin #69; the sheet does not name an opponent. A second reign for "Mr. Attitude" Jeremy Nace. The lineage is unknown after this.

Won the title by beating Hardcore Brandon Camden in the last leg of a 'Pier Six Brawl' gauntlet match in Bulletin #20 at Madison Square Garden, New York City. The gauntlet also involved Spine Snapper, Mr. Downtown, Ultimate Terror and Bloodscream.
Beat Death Jester for the vacant title in Bulletin #22 at Wrigley Field, Chicago, Illinois. Big Daddy G. had been stripped after leaving the league.
Beat Kaos Knight in Bulletin #24 at the STW Arena, Phoenix, Arizona.
Beat Spine Snapper in Bulletin #33 at the Alamo Dome, San Antonio, Texas.
Beat Mercury in Bulletin #34 at the Market Square Arena, Indianapolis, Indiana. Bloodscream was the guest referee.
Beat Avatarr the Collector in a gauntlet match in Bulletin #41 at the Civic Arena, Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. Avatarr the Collector had defeated Adrian Dango and Hypnos earlier in the same gauntlet.
Recorded as winning the title in Bulletin #53; the sheet does not name an opponent. The lineage is then unknown between Bulletin #54 and Bulletin #57.
Recorded as winning the title in Bulletin #58; the sheet does not name an opponent. A second reign for "Way Hot" Scott Colton.
Recorded as winning the title in Bulletin #62; the sheet does not name an opponent.
Recorded as winning the title in Bulletin #63; the sheet does not name an opponent.
Recorded as winning the title in Bulletin #63; the sheet does not name an opponent. A second reign for Ajax, recorded at the same bulletin number as the reign before it.
Recorded as winning the title in Bulletin #65; the sheet does not name an opponent.
Recorded as winning the title in Bulletin #69; the sheet does not name an opponent. A third reign for Ajax, marked as the last official reign of the title.
Won the title by beating Porkchop Cash in a tourney final in Bulletin #18 at the Tacoma Dome, Tacoma, Washington.
Beat Kensuki Tanaka in Bulletin #20 at Madison Square Garden, New York City.
Beat Porkchop Cash in Bulletin #21 at the San Jose Shark Tank, San Jose, California.
Beat Everlasting Torture in Bulletin #24 at the STW Arena, Phoenix, Arizona.

Beat "Dangerous" Dave Howard to win the vacant title in Bulletin #25 at the Philadelphia Spectrum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The title was then retired with Mercury as titleholder in Bulletin #27 at the STW Arena.

Beat "Mr. May" Aaron Duncan in a tourney final to win the newly reactivated title in Bulletin #35 at the Pontiac Silver Dome, Pontiac, Michigan. Cardinal Sin changed his name to Lightning Knight shortly after winning the title.
Beat Lightning Knight in Bulletin #37 at the Sun Dome, Tampa, Florida.

Beat Thanatos and Dalen Sickmiller to claim the vacant title in Bulletin #40 at the Paladium, Hollywood, California. The title had become vacant when Kabuki Dragon, Thanatos and Dalen Sickmiller all pinned champion Wandering Soul simultaneously in a five-way match in Bulletin #39.
Beat Kabuki Dragon in a Fatal 4-Way in Bulletin #41 at the Civic Arena, Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. Also involved Motoharu Kajitsu and Tommy Rush.
Beat "The Sellout" Rocky Austin in Bulletin #45 at the Alamo Dome, San Antonio, Texas.
Beat Tommy Rush in Bulletin #52.
Recorded as winning the title in Bulletin #60; the sheet does not name an opponent. A second reign for Mercury.
Recorded as winning the title in Bulletin #63; the sheet does not name an opponent. A second reign for "Ab Fab" Adam Colton.
Recorded as winning the title in Bulletin #67; the sheet does not name an opponent.

Beat Jake Rush in Bulletin #69. A third reign for "Ab Fab" Adam Colton; this win unified the title with the STW World Heavyweight Championship. The lineage is unknown after this as a stand-alone title.

Recorded as the first champion awarded the first title by a stand-in commissioner (a real name, withheld under the privacy rule) in Bulletin #44 at the Kiel Center, St. Louis, Missouri; the sheet does not name an opponent. Awarded rather than won in a match.
Beat Veronica B. in a triple threat in Bulletin #45 at the Alamo Dome, San Antonio, Texas. Also involved Pandora.
Beat Sex Goddess Sunny Beach in Bulletin #48.
Beat Cousin Becky in Bulletin #50. A second reign for Sex Goddess Sunny Beach; the lineage is then unknown between Bulletin #55 and Bulletin #57.
Recorded as winning the title in Bulletin #58; the sheet does not name an opponent. A second reign for Cousin Becky.
Recorded as the first champion in Bulletin #67; the sheet does not name an opponent.
Recorded as winning the title in Bulletin #69; the sheet does not name an opponent. The lineage is unknown after this.
Recorded as the first champion in Bulletin #69; the sheet does not name an opponent. The lineage is unknown after this.
